narrative: The model estimated a 58% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning your financial profile fell on the riskier side and the loan was denied. The strongest factor was the status of your checking account: being below zero DM was the most influential signal and pushed the decision toward bad credit; only about 12.6% of approved applicants had this status. The second strongest factor was the requested credit duration. You asked for 42 months, more than double the approved average of about 19 months, and a longer repayment period pushed the prediction toward higher risk. Your credit history was the third most influential factor. Although its value was critical/other credits, in this case its overall effect leaned toward good credit rather than bad; it was simply not enough to offset the first two factors. To improve a future application, focus on bringing your checking account into positive standing and avoiding overdrafts, and consider requesting a smaller amount or shorter repayment period. Building savings, reducing existing credit obligations, or adding a reliable co-applicant or guarantor could also strengthen your profile. You may wish to request feedback on your credit history and reapply once these areas are stronger.
